fullPassage:
Great Opening Lines

You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. But people aren't the only ones who make first impressions — books do as well. A powerful first line of a book can catch readers' attention and make them want to read on. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years coming up with the perfect opening line for their books. Let's take a look at some of them.

"All children, except one, grow up."
- Peter Pan, J.M. Barrie

No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult whether they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who refuses to grow older. He wants to have fun and stay a child forever.

One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell visit the home of Wendy, John, and Michael. Peter Pan invites them to a fantastic island in the sky called Neverland. It is a magical place where dreams are born and excitement never ends. The children take Peter Pan's hand and their adventure begins. Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.

"There is no lake at Camp Green Lake."
- Holes, Louis Sachar

What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, having a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. So what kind of place do you imagine Camp Green Lake is? Perhaps it is a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes paints a different picture. It states that there is no lake there despite its name. Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games.

In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. Stanley and the other boys at Camp Green Lake are expected to improve their character by digging holes every day. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?

"It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen."
- 1984, George Orwell

Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the ordinary. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual. Not just one clock but all clocks strike thirteen here. What's more, the number thirteen is often associated with bad luck in Western cultures. In this way, Orwell hints to the readers that they are about to enter a world that is dark and unfamiliar.

The story takes place in an imaginary country called Oceania in the year 1984. The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, watches everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never be free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with what the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by himself. Will Winston find others to join him? Or will he give in and be controlled by Big Brother like the rest of the people?

questions.passage: You never get a second chance to make a first impression. It is very important to make a good impression on others when we meet them for the first time. Authors often spend weeks, months, or even years ④<u>coming</u> up with the perfect opening line.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 첫인상을 남길 두 번째 기회는 없다. 첫인상을 남기는 것은 사람만이 아니다. 책의 강렬한 첫 문장은 독자들의 관심을 사로잡고 계속 읽고 ③싶게 만든다. 작가들은 완벽한 첫 문장을 ④생각해 내는 데 수주~수년이 걸린다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ wanting → want: 'make + O + V(원형)' 사역동사 구문. make them want to read on. wanting(현재분사)은 사역동사 뒤에 부적절. ✅ ① who: 관계대명사(선행사 ones=people). ✅ ② catch: can catch 정상. ✅ ④ coming: spend time -ing 정상.
det.tip: 사역동사 make + O + V(원형): ~가 …하게 만들다. spend time -ing: ~하는 데 시간을 쓰다

questions.passage: No one can stop the sands of time. Every child becomes an adult ①<u>whether</u> they want to or not. But the opening line of Peter Pan states that there is one child who is the exception to the rule. Peter Pan is a boy who ②<u>refuses</u> to grow older. He wants to have fun and ③<u>stays</u> a child forever. One night in London, Peter Pan and Tinker Bell ④<u>visit</u> the home of Wendy, John, and Michael.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 세월의 흐름을 멈출 수 없다. 모든 어린이는 ①원하든 원하지 않든 어른이 된다. 피터 팬은 나이 드는 것을 ②거부하는 소년이다. 즐겁게 ③지내며 아이로 남고 싶어 한다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ stays → stay: 'wants to have fun and stay'에서 to에 연결된 병렬 구조. wants to have and (to) stay. stays(3인칭 단수)는 to 뒤에 부적절. ✅ ① whether: ~이든 아니든. ✅ ② refuses: 3인칭 단수 정상. ✅ ④ visit: 복수 주어 정상.
det.tip: want to A and (to) B: A하고 B하고 싶다. to 뒤에는 동사 원형.

questions.passage: What comes to mind when you hear the word "camp?" Many people would think of fun activities like fishing, ①<u>having</u> a barbecue, and sleeping under the beautiful stars. Perhaps it is a beautiful place ②<u>which</u> a green forest surrounds a blue lake. But the first line of Holes ③<u>paints</u> a different picture. It states that there is no lake there ④<u>despite</u> its name.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 캠프라는 단어를 들으면? 낚시하기, 바비큐 ①해 먹기 등 재미있는 활동을 떠올릴 것이다. 초록빛 숲이 호수를 둘러싼 아름다운 곳일 것이다. 하지만 첫 문장은 ③다른 그림을 그린다. 이름에도 ④불구하고 호수가 없다.
det.analysis: ❌ ② which → where: 'a beautiful place where a green forest surrounds' — 장소를 수식하는 관계부사 where. which 뒤에는 불완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 'a green forest surrounds a blue lake'는 완전한 문장. ✅ ① having: 병렬(-ing) 정상. ✅ ③ paints: 단수 주어 정상. ✅ ④ despite: 전치사 정상.
det.tip: 장소 선행사 + where + 완전한 문장. which는 주어/목적어 빠진 불완전한 문장 앞에.

questions.passage: The government tries to control everyone's life. It has even created a new language to limit people's thoughts and expressions. Big Brother, the leader of Oceania, ①<u>watches</u> everything that goes on through television screens. As long as Big Brother is in power, the people of Oceania will never ②<u>be</u> free. The main character, Winston Smith, does not agree with ③<u>that</u> the government is doing. He wants to fight against Big Brother, but he can't do it by ④<u>himself</u>.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 정부는 모든 사람의 생활을 통제한다. 빅 브라더는 모든 일을 ①지켜본다. 집권하는 한 결코 ②자유롭지 못할 것이다. 윈스턴은 정부가 하는 일에 동의하지 않는다. 혼자서는 할 수 없다.
det.analysis: ❌ ③ that → what: 'agree with what the government is doing'에서 what은 '~하는 것'(선행사 포함 관계대명사). that은 agree with의 목적어 역할 불가(뒤에 완전한 문장이면 접속사 that이지만, is doing의 목적어가 빠져 불완전). ✅ ① watches: 3인칭 단수 정상. ✅ ② be: will never be 정상. ✅ ④ himself: 재귀대명사(주어 he) 정상.
det.tip: what = the thing that: ~하는 것. agree with what S + V: S가 V하는 것에 동의하다

questions.passage: In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. The main character of the book, a teenage boy named Stanley Yelnats, is different from the other boys in the camp. He hasn't done anything wrong. He was just in the wrong place at the wrong time. questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 초록 호수 캠프는 사막의 감옥이다. 주인공 스탠리는 잘못한 것이 없다. 스탠리는 구덩이 파기에 다른 이유가 있다고 의심한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② suspects: '의심하다'. 확실하지 않지만 다른 이유가 있을 거라 추측. ❌ ① confirms(확인하다): 확실한 건 아님. ❌ ③ denies(부인하다): 반대. ❌ ④ announces(발표하다): 부적절.
det.tip: suspect: 의심하다 (= have a feeling that)

questions.passage: Typically, clocks strike from one to twelve times. But George Orwell's well-known novel, 1984, opens with the clocks striking thirteen times. In a normal world, a clock striking thirteen is out of the __________. But in this mysterious place, it doesn't seem to be unusual.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 보통 시계는 12번까지 친다. 1984는 13번 치는 시계로 시작한다. 정상 세계에서 13번 치는 것은 비범한 것이다. 하지만 이 불가사의한 곳에서는 특별해 보이지 않는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ④ ordinary: 'out of the ordinary'(비범한, 보통이 아닌) 관용구. ❌ ①②③ out of the question/control/sight는 다른 관용구.
det.tip: out of the ordinary: 비범한, 보통이 아닌 (= unusual, extraordinary)

"사람뿐 아니라 책도 첫인상을 남긴다."

det.korean: 첫인상을 남기는 것은 사람만이 아니다 — 책 역시 그렇다.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 'people aren't the only ones — books do as well'에서 직접 확인.

det.korean: 스탠리는 캠프의 다른 소년들과는 다르다. 잘못한 것이 없다. 잘못된 장소에 잘못된 시간에 있었을 뿐이다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 'is different from the other boys'이고 'hasn't done anything wrong'. 나쁜 행동을 해서 온 것이 아님.

det.analysis: ✅ ① grow up: '성장하다'. 네버랜드에서는 아이로 남는다는 맥락. ❌ ② wake up(일어나다): 무관. ❌ ③ give up(포기하다): 무관. ❌ ④ show up(나타나다): 무관.

det.analysis: ✅ ③ dark: 불운·불가사의한 분위기에 '어두운'. and unfamiliar와 어조 일치. ❌ ① bright(밝은): 반대. ❌ ② peaceful(평화로운): 부적절. ❌ ④ ordinary(평범한): out of the ordinary와 모순.

ch: 피터 팬은 빨리 어른이 되고 싶어 한다.

det.korean: 피터 팬은 나이 드는 것을 거부한다. 팅커벨과 함께 웬디의 집에 방문한다. 네버랜드는 꿈이 만들어지고 신나는 일이 끝없는 마법의 장소이다.

스탠리는 나쁜 행동을 해서 캠프에 보내졌다.

det.korean: 사막에 위치. 스탠리는 잘못한 것이 없고 잘못된 장소에 있었을 뿐. 매일 구덩이를 판다. 캠프가 아니다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② 불일치: 'hasn't done anything wrong'에서 나쁜 행동을 한 것이 아님. ❌ ①③④ 일치.
det.tip: hasn't done anything wrong: 잘못한 것이 없다

ch: 독자를 사로잡는 소설의 인상적인 첫 문장들

det.korean: 첫인상을 남기는 것은 사람만이 아니라 책도 그렇다. 강렬한 첫 문장이 독자의 관심을 사로잡는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ② 본문은 3권의 소설(Peter Pan, Holes, 1984)의 인상적인 첫 문장을 소개. ❌ ①③④ 부분적이거나 무관.
det.tip: opening line: 첫 문장, catch readers' attention: 독자의 관심을 사로잡다

questions.passage: Through this irony, Sachar is hinting that Camp Green Lake is not a normal camp with fun and games. In fact, Camp Green Lake is not a camp at all. Located in the desert, it is like a prison for bad boys. Stanley suspects that there is another reason for the digging. Will Stanley successfully dig up the truth about Camp Green Lake?
questions.stem: 위 글의 핵심 내용을 가장 잘 요약한 것은?
ch: 이름과 다른 캠프의 진실을 파헤치는 이야기
호수에서 낚시하며 즐기는 여름 캠프 이야기

det.korean: 이름에도 불구하고 호수가 없고 사막의 감옥이다. 스탠리는 구덩이 파기의 진짜 이유를 의심한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③ 이름(Green Lake)과 현실(사막 감옥)의 괴리, 숨겨진 진실. ❌ ①②④ 원문과 불일치.
det.tip: dig up the truth: 진실을 파헤치다 (dig의 이중 의미 — 구덩이 파기/진실 파기)

questions.passage: Only children can visit Neverland, and they do not grow up as long as they remain there. They have a wonderful time in Neverland. What is the reason for this unexpected decision? Read the book to find out.
questions.stem:
다음 한국어 문장을 본문의 표현을 활용하여 영어로 옮기시오.

"결국 세 아이는 집으로 돌아가서 성장하기로 결심한다."

※ But in the end으로 시작할 것
questions.wa: But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up.

det.korean: But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up.
det.analysis: in the end(결국) + the three children(세 아이) + decide to(결심하다) + return home and grow up(돌아가서 성장하다).
det.tip: in the end: 결국 (= finally), decide to V: ~하기로 결심하다

questions.ans: But in the end, the three children decide to return home and grow up.
